title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Graph API options for icons, visibility, metadata and labels on custom connectors
summary: Hold: the controls table reports no admin UI for assigning semantic labels to custom connectors, but Microsoft documents that UI for SDK-built custom connectors. Narrow that row to connectors built directly with the Graph API; the roadmap facts, visibility path and schema API are supported.

claims.claim: A developer can build a custom connector with the Copilot connectors API to index their own data source.
claims.quote: You might want to build a custom connector to integrate with services that aren't available as connectors built by Microsoft. To build custom connectors, you use the Copilot connectors REST API.

claims.claim: The options are developer-facing.
claims.quote: Developers can now configure icons, visibility settings, connection metadata, property descriptions, and semantic labels for custom connectors.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for semantic labels and property descriptions in a custom connector's schema.
claims.quote: When you use the Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors ... SDK, you can publish your custom connectors through the Microsoft 365 admin center ... On the Assign property labels page, assign semantic labels to your source properties.
claims.fix: Narrow controls[1].governs and its rendered table text to 'Semantic labels and property descriptions in a custom connector built directly with the Graph API (not the SDK)'. Retain ui: null for that narrower case. Add to its note: 'SDK-built custom connectors have an Assign property labels page during admin-center publishing.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/custom-connector-sdk-publish.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/external/connections/{id}/schema creates or updates the schema with description and labels on its properties, including iconUrl mappings.
claims.quote: Create a new or update an existing schema ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/contosohr/schema ... In the request body, supply a JSON representation of a schema object.
